title: En virtud de: la base legal de una acción

sections.content: En virtud de (by virtue of, under) introduces the formal legal or official basis for an action -- common in historical writing about laws, decrees, and institutions. It's followed by a noun phrase, and often carries a slightly skeptical edge when the "legal basis" cited is itself questionable. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: El estado de sitio suspendía derechos constitucionales básicos, en virtud de una supuesta emergencia nacional.
items.english: The state of siege suspended basic constitutional rights, by virtue of a supposed national emergency.

items.spanish: En virtud de estos decretos, las fuerzas de seguridad podían detener a cualquier persona sin necesidad de una orden judicial.
items.english: By virtue of these decrees, security forces could detain any person without needing a judicial order.

items.spanish: En virtud de su supuesta legalidad, el régimen presentaba estas medidas como una simple respuesta a una amenaza real.
items.english: By virtue of their supposed legality, the regime presented these measures as a simple response to a real threat.

items.spanish: En virtud del control que ejercía sobre el poder judicial, el régimen se aseguraba de que ningún tribunal cuestionara estas prácticas.
items.english: By virtue of the control it exercised over the judiciary, the regime made sure no court would question these practices.

sections.content: En virtud de is more formal than por or debido a -- reach for it specifically when the reading needs to name the legal or official justification behind an action, not just any general cause.
